summary: 纽约治理涂鸦的政策把注意力放在破坏行为上，作者则追溯涂鸦作为青年文化和艺术表达的历史，主张用合法创作空间区分并回应不同类型的涂鸦。
logic: 追溯青年文化和广告环境

paragraphs.brief: 破窗理论与纽约涂鸦政策
sentences: Spray-painted graffiti can be seen on city walls or on trains in many cities, and New York is no exception.
在许多城市，建筑墙面或列车上都能看到喷漆涂鸦，纽约也不例外。
Since the late eighties, New York City’s policy on graffiti has been based on the ‘broken windows’ thesis.
自二十世纪八十年代末起，纽约市的涂鸦政策一直以“破窗理论”为基础。
This theory, introduced in 1982 in Atlantic Monthly by James Q Wilson and George L Kelling, argues that petty, non-violent crimes such as the creation of graffiti increase overall crime.
詹姆斯·威尔逊和乔治·凯林于1982年在《大西洋月刊》阐述这一理论，认为涂鸦之类轻微的非暴力违法行为会使整体犯罪增多。
The theory reasons that if minor signs of disorder such as broken windows and graffiti are left unfixed, potential criminals assume that chaos reigns, and commit more crimes.
该理论认为，破窗和涂鸦之类的小规模失序迹象若得不到处理，潜在违法者便会以为这里无人管理，从而犯下更多罪行。
As Lieutenant Steve Mona of the New York City Vandal Squad stated in his anti-graffiti program, ‘Graffiti gives the look of disorder, as if nobody is in control.
纽约市反破坏公物小组的史蒂夫·莫纳警官在反涂鸦计划中说：“涂鸦给人一种失序的印象，仿佛没有人管。
Graffiti is the first sign that a neighborhood is falling apart.’
涂鸦是社区开始衰败的第一个迹象。”
paragraphs.gist: 纽约自八十年代末依据“破窗理论”治理涂鸦，理由是未处理的小规模失序会让人觉得无人管理，从而鼓励更多犯罪。

paragraphs.brief: 治安改善能否归功于清除涂鸦
sentences: New York has spent a large amount of time and money fighting graffiti in the belief that these efforts will send a message that there is someone in charge, and overall crime will fall.
纽约投入大量时间和金钱清除涂鸦，相信这能传递出“这里有人管理”的信号，从而降低整体犯罪率。
However, while the application of the ‘broken windows’ thesis is credited by some as causing the fall in crime in New York, there is little evidence supporting this.
然而，虽然有人把纽约犯罪率的下降归功于“破窗理论”的运用，支持这种因果关系的证据却很少。
Instead, many criminologists attribute the reduction in crime to a collection of causes, only one of which is the attention to small, visible crime by the police.
许多犯罪学家认为，犯罪减少有多种原因，警方关注显而易见的轻微犯罪只是其中之一。
However, of these small crimes, graffiti still gets a particularly bad rap from the New York City Transit Authority.
不过，在这类轻微违法行为中，纽约市交通管理局对涂鸦尤其反感。
According to its website, ‘Graffiti has long been viewed as the most obvious sign of urban blight.’
该局网站称：“长久以来，涂鸦一直被视为城市衰败最明显的标志。”

Reasons for concern expressed by the Mayor of New York about the presence of graffiti include the belief that graffiti is a threat to the ‘quality of life’ in the city, and that it leads to greater acts of crime.
纽约市长担心，涂鸦会损害城市生活品质，也可能招致更严重的犯罪行为。
The Mayor also argues that it causes millions of dollars of damage to property holders and to the city, and that graffiti ‘tags’ (decorated initials) are a means of communication for gangs.
市长还认为，涂鸦给业主和市政府造成了数百万美元损失，而涂鸦签名，也就是装饰过的姓名首字母，成了帮派联络的手段。
paragraphs.gist: 市政当局把涂鸦与财产损失、帮派和生活品质联系起来，但犯罪下降究竟有多少归功于整治小案，犯罪学家并没有充分证据。

paragraphs.brief: 一概排斥掩盖艺术差异
sentences: While the Mayor’s contentions are valid, they only apply to the most degenerate types of graffiti.
市长的说法虽有道理，却只适用于性质最恶劣的一类涂鸦。
City administrators lump together all forms of graffiti: artistic, meaningful, and gang-or drug-related, into one undesirable group.
市政管理者把各种涂鸦一概当作不受欢迎的东西，无论是有艺术性或有意义的作品，还是与帮派、毒品有关的标记。
This oversimplifies the realities of street art.
这过分简化了街头艺术的现实。

Graffiti artist Dmitri Wright comments: ‘Graffiti has a multitude of forms and meanings but a lot of the connotations of the art form and how it is linked to street culture create a divide … All its opponents need to do is look at some of it.
涂鸦艺术家德米特里·赖特说：“涂鸦的形式和意义多种多样，但这门艺术带来的许多联想，以及它与街头文化的关系，会造成人们的隔阂……反对者其实只需看看其中一些作品。
It is absolutely spectacular, but sometimes people can’t get past their own culture.’
它们实在精彩得很，可有时候人们走不出自己的文化视角。”
paragraphs.gist: 把帮派符号、有社会意义的表达和艺术创作一概归为有害涂鸦，会掩盖街头艺术的形式差异，也可能让人因文化成见而错过作品。

paragraphs.brief: 涂鸦艺术的市场和城市价值
sentences: The beautiful graffiti-art that can be found today throughout the city, on commissioned walls and in art galleries, is an expression of New York like no other art form.
从受托绘制的墙面到艺术画廊，如今在全城可见的精美涂鸦作品，用其他艺术形式所没有的方式表达着纽约。
Its artists either come from the city itself, or are drawn to the city from around the world.
创作者有的就来自纽约，有的从世界各地被这座城市吸引而来。
Surely, in the right context, graffiti-art can become a powerful tool to promote New York City’s identity and originality.
在适当场合，涂鸦艺术可以有力展现纽约这座城市的特色与原创力。

Although graffiti first emerged as an illegal form of expression, its influence on the art world is increasingly present, and many large-scale pieces are impressive not only in their size, but also in their artistic themes and techniques.
虽然涂鸦首先成为一种非法表达形式，但涂鸦对艺术界的影响日益明显，许多大型作品不仅在大小方面，而且在艺术主题和技术方面，都令人印象深刻。
Today, New York graffiti-art on canvas can sell for tens of thousands of dollars.
如今，纽约创作在画布上的涂鸦艺术作品可以卖到数万美元。
paragraphs.gist: 受托墙画与画廊作品吸引世界各地的创作者，既展现纽约独特的城市身份，也因技法和主题在艺术市场上获得高价。

paragraphs.brief: 青年借墙面表达并成名
sentences: Graffiti New York-style has its roots in a social movement of young people in the seventies and eighties, and the themes in graffiti-art were undeniably a reflection of social factors at play in New York.
纽约式涂鸦起源于七八十年代的青年社会运动，作品主题无疑反映了当时纽约社会中的种种因素。
The city’s youths wanted to speak out about the issues that affected them and have their messages heard.
纽约的年轻人想说出切身关心的问题，也希望有人听到他们的声音。
Kids with nothing more than ingenuity could gain recognition as minor celebrities.
哪怕手中只有才华与巧思，孩子也可能因此成为小有名气的人物。
Graffiti artist King Bee explains: ‘In the world of graffiti, every writer or artist, one way or another, participates in the fame game.
艺术家King Bee说：“在涂鸦的世界里，每个写手或画家或多或少都在争取名声。
They all seek recognition for their creativity in the who’s who in the graffiti game.’
他们都希望自己的创意得到涂鸦圈内知名人物的认可。”
paragraphs.gist: 纽约式涂鸦源于七八十年代的青年运动，年轻人借墙面表达切身议题，也让仅靠创意的人有机会在同辈中赢得声名。

paragraphs.brief: 满城广告与青年自我推介
sentences: Graffiti grew in part out of a reaction to the fact that the city was becoming covered in advertisements.
涂鸦之所以越来越多，部分是年轻人对满城广告作出的回应。
City administrators did not see the connection between the rise of advertising saturating the landscape, and the increasing saturation of the city with graffiti.
城市管理者没有看到广告的兴起与城市涂鸦日益饱和之间的联系。
It was a natural progression that the youth of the day would use the same tools to sell themselves that the corporations were using to sell products to the public.
企业用公共视觉媒介向大众推销商品，当时的年轻人用同样手段推介自己，也是很自然的发展。
paragraphs.gist: 城市广告占满视野也推动了涂鸦兴起，年轻人借企业推销商品所用的公共视觉语言来展示自己，管理者却忽略了这种联系。

paragraphs.brief: 以合法创作空间代替一味禁止
sentences: When considering approaches to the graffiti issue, there should be more productive ways to combat graffiti than simply banning it.
面对涂鸦，应该有比一味禁止更有成效的办法。
The most common alternative suggested is creating a legitimate outlet for the graffiti urges of young people.
最常见的建议，是给年轻人想画涂鸦的冲动提供一个合法的出口。
Private groups such as The Phun Phactory have put this concept into action.
民间团体Phun Phactory等已经把这个想法付诸实践。

Pat DiLillo, founder of The Phun Phactory, explains the logic behind his organization: ‘I figured if I created a place for the young people to paint [graffiti], then it would eliminate the illegal graffiti … Many of these artists start out as vandals.
涂鸦场地 Phun Phactory 的创办人帕特·迪利洛这样解释初衷：“我想，如果给年轻人一个可以合法画涂鸦的地方，非法涂鸦就会消失……这些艺术家中，很多人起初是以破坏公物的方式作画的。”
There is nothing for them to do; there’s no youth program or anything.’
“他们没有事情可做，既没有青少年活动计划，也没有别的去处。”
paragraphs.gist: 单纯禁画之外，一些民间团体为年轻人提供合法墙面和活动空间，希望有创作出口便能减少非法涂写。

paragraphs.brief: 通过公共艺术连结年轻人
sentences: Many graffiti pieces in the city, far from being related to juvenile delinquency, are dedicated to powerful social issues.
城中许多作品与青少年违法无关，反而着眼于重大的社会问题。

Though their messages may be the same, ties between the city and graffiti artists are rarely sought and never formed, although many socially influenced pieces display the potential for creating such bonds.
市政府和涂鸦艺术家想传达的意思或许相近，但双方很少主动建立联系，也始终没有形成纽带，尽管许多受社会问题启发的作品已显示这种可能。
By providing a legal medium for the artistic impulses of the city’s youth, the city could form a relationship with that generation as well as gain a beautified urban environment.
如果让城市青年通过合法渠道表达艺术冲动，市政府既能与他们建立联系，也能让市容更美。
paragraphs.gist: 不少作品关注重大的社会议题，市政府若给年轻人的表达提供合法载体，既可能改善城市景观，也能与这一代人建立联系。

correct: crime rates rise unless small offences are dealt with.
若不处理轻微违法行为，犯罪率就会上升。

items.en: The writer states that graffiti started in New York because
items.zh: 作者认为，涂鸦为什么会在纽约兴起？
correct: young people adopted the publicity tactics of companies.
年轻人采取了公司的宣传策略。

items.en: According to Pat DiLillo, what is the answer to New York’s graffiti problem?
items.zh: 帕特·迪利洛认为，怎样可以解决纽约的涂鸦问题？

items.en: In the final paragraph, the writer recommends that the city authorities should
items.zh: 在最后一段，作者建议市政府怎么做？
correct: develop a connection with graffiti artists.
与涂鸦艺术家建立联系。

items.en: There is clear proof that the application of the ‘broken windows’ theory led to a lower crime rate in New York.
items.zh: 有明确证据表明，应用“破窗理论”使纽约的犯罪率下降。
items.why: 有些人把犯罪率下降归功于“破窗理论”，但作者随即指出支持这种因果关系的证据很少，与“有明确证据”相反。

items.en: City administrators fail to distinguish between graffiti as vandalism and graffiti-art.
items.zh: 市政管理者没有把蓄意破坏公物的涂鸦与涂鸦艺术区分开来。
items.why: 作者说市政府把艺术性涂鸦、有意义的表达和涉帮派或毒品的涂鸦归为同一类问题，正是没有区分艺术与破坏。

items.en: The graffiti-art that can be found in New York is of the highest standard in the world.
items.zh: 纽约的涂鸦艺术达到了世界最高水平。
items.why: 创作者有纽约本地人，也有来自世界各地的人。艺术家的来源很广，却不能据此推断纽约涂鸦的水平排名全球第一。

items.en: Graffiti might be an important way of raising New York’s profile as a unique city.
items.zh: 涂鸦或许是提升纽约独特城市形象的重要途径。
items.why: 作者认为，在适当场合，涂鸦艺术可以有力地展现纽约的身份和原创性，正好支持它能突出这座城市的独特形象。

items.en: Graffiti has had minimal impact on the art world.
items.zh: 涂鸦对艺术界的影响微乎其微。
items.why: 原文说涂鸦在艺术界的影响越来越明显。“影响微乎其微”与作者所述的增长趋势和实际影响不符。

groups.label: 观点判断 · YES / NO / NOT GIVEN

items.answer: B · graffiti creates an impression that the law is not being obeyed in the community
items.solution: 涂鸦给人留下的印象是，法律在社区中得不到遵守

items.en: The Mayor of New York states that
items.answer: H · graffiti results in great monetary cost to New York and its citizens
items.solution: 涂鸦会给纽约及其公民带来巨大的金钱损失

items.en: Graffiti artist Dmitri Wright thinks that
items.zh: 涂鸦艺术家德米特里·赖特认为……
items.answer: E · some individuals do not see the beauty of graffiti because of their backgrounds
items.solution: 有些人受自身背景影响，欣赏不到涂鸦的美。

items.en: King Bee is a New York graffiti artist who believes
items.zh: 纽约涂鸦艺术家 King Bee 认为……
items.answer: G · graffiti artists are motivated by the need to have their work acknowledged
items.solution: 涂鸦艺术家创作的动力，是希望自己的作品得到认可。

items.en: Pat DiLillo of the Phun Phactory claims
items.zh: Phun Phactory 的帕特·迪利洛认为……
items.answer: F · teenagers lack suitable ways to spend their time
items.solution: 青少年缺少合适的消遣方式。

pairs: created a place for the young people to paint
题目概括为划定涂鸦区，迪利洛的原话是给年轻人建一处可以作画的地方。
题目说损失巨大，市长用数百万美元的损失说明代价有多高。
第 5 段 · 第 3 句
points: 原文说涂鸦在艺术界的影响越来越明显。“影响微乎其微”与作者所述的增长趋势和实际影响不符。
题干问“纽约市长说”。定位句写到“市长还说，这给财产持有者和城市造成了数百万美元的损失，涂鸦 " 标签 " (装饰名)是帮派的通讯手段”。
clauses: This theory, introduced in 1982 in Atlantic Monthly by James Q Wilson and George L Kelling, argues ….
“that petty, non-violent crimes such as the creation of graffiti increase overall crime”补足 argues 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 argues 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
The theory reasons that …, potential criminals assume that chaos reigns, and commit more crimes.
连接词 if 引出“if minor signs of disorder such as broken windows and graffiti are left unfixed”，说明主句的条件关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 if 把这一层关系补进去。
